correctness.rationale: Correctness: Fourier inversion exactly supplies three cyclic autocorrelations. Zero-lag Hankel determinant separates 0/1/2-sparse strata; the nonantipodal ratio supplies the ordinary support sum and a quadratic recovers both support weights; the antipodal half-period chirp reads the missing imaginary phase. For two possible antipodal supports, exact factorization of distinct candidate squared chirped-lag magnitudes proves they cannot coincide. Positive weights and all phase boundary cases, including zero real product, are treated. Symbolic identity independently verified with SymPy and standard-library checker passed 3678 two-sparse cases plus 18 exact rational identities. Finite checks are supplementary, not all-N proof.

originality.rationale: Originality: the closest fully inspected published Fourier statement proves two positive masks only in odd dimensions and explicitly says that its real-mask even impossibility does not rule out complex masks. Here three bounded-contrast masks, including a half-Nyquist phase-coded mask, identify every complex two-sparse vector in every even dimension uniformly, overcoming that exact missing parity case. The 2026 probabilistic full-signal O(log N)-mask PhaseLift theorem does not imply a uniform deterministic three-mask guarantee, as its own Theorem 1 notes its nonuniform fixed-signal quantifier. Older works use random many-mask or continuous-space three-mask settings. Absence of indexed matching text alone is not novelty proof; earlier unindexed equivalent special-case designs remain possible.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed special-purpose finite two-sparse Fourier mask construction may be equivalent under a nonobvious reduction.
The full 2021 Li–Li article and full Jaming–Rathmair article were not read; assessments of their scope beyond accessible abstracts/tables remain limited.
Bibliographic searches and accessible ledger claims cannot establish global novelty.

value.rationale: Value: complex two-sparse Fourier phase retrieval is the first nontrivial unknown-support phaseless recovery case. Real masks intrinsically lose the imaginary component of antipodal correlations in every even cycle; an explicit all-N fixed-cardinality, bounded-gain complex design removes that structural blind spot and supplies a completely constructive decoder. The nontrivial two-candidate weighted-moment factorization gives a meaningful guarantee rather than a routine reparametrization. No optimal count or larger-sparsity claim is made.
